study.question: Does restoring the fresh context map's Frobenius norm rescue rank35 capacity reduction, or does exact full-rank factorization already incur a quality loss under the fixed training recipe?
study.hypothesis: Observed: dense separate context gives click AUC0.6672902815744913, dense192883, train319.997s, inference25.442s, model batch p50/p95=15.201/15.323ms. Raw rank35 gives0.6669746715660667, dense182019, train313.383s, inference24.552s, p50/p95=15.030/15.106ms. Rank48 gives0.6666401850657749, dense185971, train319.559s, inference26.030s. Nonmonotonic quality and inconsistent timing do not establish rank necessity or efficiency. Mechanism hypothesis: truncating an untrained map reduces its initial energy and changes buy-to-context optimization, contributing to the rank35 click loss; restoring only global energy may preserve click quality with identical reduced storage/forward cost. Exact full-rank factors test whether factorized optimization itself changes quality without discarded singular directions. This is unverified and does not assert novelty.
